existing_terminology:

existing_identificationCriteria:
Placement in a SEN programme is conditional on the degree of disability
The programme is for pupils who require additional support services
General schools with SEN programmes cater to mild to moderate disability
The Ministry of Health is responsible for early identification and intervention
existing_referralPathway:
ECCD referral processes are called ad hoc and unsustainable without structural support
School health screening runs twice a year for health problems including disabilities
Teachers use an identification and referral system linking children to intervention centres
ECCD centres are entry points for early identification and referral to intervention
existing_serviceModel:
The 2017 inclusive education standards require schools to coordinate external support
Speech therapists are named as possible collaborators, not as school staff
The provision is permissive, 'may include', rather than an entitlement
existing_legalEntitlement:
2008 Constitution guarantees free education for all children up to tenth grade
The government has yet to ratify the CRPD or establish a national education law
2012 special educational needs policy asserts education on an equal basis with others
2019 education policy, still draft, promises specialised support and trained personnel
existing_funding:
Most health and some referral services are free, as is basic education
A separate budget line for disabled children's education rises 5.3 per cent a year
School funding is computed on child count and severity of disabilities
The 2012 special needs education policy promises adequate budget support to schools
existing_workforce:
How far disability-inclusive education is in teacher training would need further research
Two colleges of education make a special needs module compulsory in the BEd
An introductory inclusive education module is optional for pre-service secondary teachers
A long-term capacity strategy for SEN teachers is still a plan in the 2018-2028 roadmap

Jhingran, D., Early Literacy and Multilingual Education in South Asia, UNICEF Regional Office for South Asia (2019), ss. 2.1.5 and 3.2.5 (Internet Archive raw-document copy)

existing_terminology:
The umbrella term is students with complex learning profiles, not a disorder label
Its nearest category to DLD is students with hearing or speech impairment
Speech is paired with hearing; no category covers language difficulty on its own
The named learning disabilities are dyslexia, dysgraphia and dyscalculia; language is absent
Fixed in the Inclusive Education Policy, classifying from Regulation 54-R/2021
existing_identificationCriteria:
Children are assessed before enrolment using a growth monitoring card
They are categorised by severity of disability, then placed by ability
existing_multilingualProvision:
Evidence is a regional literacy review, about schooling language, not assessment
Dhivehi is declared the official language in the constitution
English is introduced from preschool and is the main medium of instruction
No option of education through the national language is offered, unlike other Asian contexts
existing_referralPathway:
A child found to have a special need is referred on to other professionals to evaluate
The mapping records the referral process itself as unclear
A hospital in Male has referral services and a child growth monitoring department
existing_serviceModel:
Speech therapy is delivered as a medical intervention, not as school support
Provision is largely by international NGOs or private providers
The mapping records no transfer of therapy into classroom learning support
existing_legalEntitlement:
Law 8/2010 mandates education without discrimination and equipment to remove learning barriers
2008 Constitution art. 7a bars discrimination on the ground of mental and physical disability
All public schools are mandated by law to cater to disabled children; only some in fact do
Ministry of Education delivers the service and supervises the inclusive education programme
existing_funding:
Resources are allocated on enrolment, and SEN children are 2.1 per cent of enrolment
SEN therefore gets the second lowest proportion of the education budget
A separate SEN line in the sector plan costing model covers salaries, equipment, training
existing_workforce:
Figures come from a UNICEF regional mapping study, not from a ministry register
185 of 212 government schools catered to children with disabilities as of 2017
A SEN unit commonly has one dedicated SEN teacher and a classroom space
Identification is particularly challenging on limited specialist skills in the country
Few rehabilitation and intervention programmes exist, for want of specialists

Any disabilities found are then recorded in the national register

LITMUS sentence repetition (SRep) task for Syrian Arabic

SRep reported highly sensitive and specific; LITMUS built for multilingual children

existing_referralPathway:
Less severe disability is integrated in public schools on Ministry of Education criteria

existing_serviceModel:
No speech and language service of any kind is recorded in the cited sources

existing_legalEntitlement:

existing_funding:
